title: Triangulatedness after derived-quotient precomposition
statement: For l, E, L, ι, X and the chosen scalar functor of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], there exists a coherent shift c on integralScalarExtensionOfUniverses l E L ι X for which DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ integralScalarExtensionOfUniverses l E L ι X is triangulated.

proof.text: Express the scalar complex as the cone of 1-s on the termwise product of the ordinary scalar functors, followed by shift [-1]. The product-complex comparison is natural and intertwines 1-s. Apply the termwise-cone homotopy exactness theorem and then the triangulated shift and homotopy-to-derived quotient.

Resolve every complex functorially by a flat-term K-flat complex. The scalar well-definedness theorem shows that scalar complexes invert quasi-isomorphisms between these representatives; lift homotopy morphisms through the full homotopy quotient and use the natural comparison to obtain the required isomorphism condition.

Apply leftDerived_from_resolvingClass to the exact homotopy functor. Its counit is invertible on the good representatives, hence gives a normalized comparison for the derived functor. The uniqueness clause of integralScalarExtensionWellDefined identifies it with the selected scalar functor. Transport the exact shift along that isomorphism and compose with Qh.

statement_change.old_statement: For l, E, L, ι, X and any CommShift c on integralScalarExtensionOfUniverses l E L ι X, the composite DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ integralScalarExtensionOfUniverses l E L ι X is IsTriangulated with the induced shift.
statement_change.what: Coherence of a shift comparison does not imply exactness. Twist an exact comparison by (-1)^n. For identity coefficient extension at l=3 on complete coefficient modules, the triangle of the nonsplit sequence Z_3 --3--> Z_3 --> F_3 has nonzero connecting class delta. The twisted comparison sends its last arrow to -delta with the first two arrows fixed; since 2 delta is nonzero this is not distinguished. The blueprint requires existence of an exact shift, not exactness for every coherent shift.
